chunks: And it was narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār, who said:
I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: "A slave was emancipated on the Day of ʿArafah." He said: "If he reaches one of the two standing places, then he has attained the hajj."

key_terms.أُعْتِقَ: was emancipated or freed from slavery
key_terms.الْحَجَّ: the hajj pilgrimage, here meaning the legally sufficient pilgrimage
key_terms.الْمَوْقِفَيْنِ: the two ritual stations, meaning ʿArafah and al-Mashʿar
key_terms.مَمْلُوكٌ: a slave or owned person whose legal status affects obligation
key_terms.يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ: the Day of ʿArafah during hajj

ai.seo_question: If a slave is freed on the Day of ʿArafah, does his hajj count as the Hajj of Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a slave who is freed on the Day of ʿArafah and whether his hajj counts as the Hajj of Islam. The Imam عليه السلام states that if he reaches one of the two prescribed stations, his hajj is considered valid and sufficient.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2892 - It was narrated from Mu'awiyah ibn Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (as): "A servant was freed on the Day of Arafah."
Imam (as) said: "If he reaches one of the two stations (Arafah or Muzdalifah), then he has caught the Hajj."
